answer: Sybil resistance here rests on collateral-weighted identity: an agent must post a bond that other agents can slash, and its vote or payout is weighted by that bond plus a slow-established reputation, not by headcount. Forging a thousand fresh identities means funding a thousand separate stakes, each observed on the ledger before it earns trust. Fabricating peers changes nothing, since peers never stand on an equal terrace; unbacked ones score at the nadir. Every honest voyage from new to trusted prices sybils out: the attacker's cost scales with identities while their reward stays flat.
